title: Eval result
description: The structured result of one eval suite run against one system version, filed against its registry entry. Exactly the shape published in chapter 05 (suite_id, model_version, score, threshold, result, timestamp), with optional fields for direction, failure mode and provenance.
$comment: AI Governance Engineer templates and schemas library, v1. CC BY 4.0 (attribution: Jorge García Aibar). x-evidences names the obligations a field or record helps evidence: an illustrative mapping, not a claim of conformity and not legal advice. https://aigovernanceengineer.com/resources/templates

$schema.description: The URI of this schema, so a record says what it claims to be.

suite_id.description: Versioned id of the eval suite (for example "injection-resistance.v4").

model_version.description: The system or model tested, as "id@version" from the registry.

threshold.description: The threshold the score is compared with, traced to a failure mode or obligation.

result.description: Pass or fail against the threshold. A fail blocks the pipeline.

direction.description: How the score compares with the threshold.

metric.description: Name of the metric the score measures.

failure_mode.description: The failure mode or harm the suite tests for.

obligation.description: The obligation the threshold traces to, if any (for example "EU AI Act Art. 15").

sample_size.description: Number of test cases in the run.

input_hash.description: Digest of the suite and dataset snapshot used.

signature.description: Detached signature over the record, prefixed with the algorithm (for example "ed25519:<base64>"). Makes the record tamper-evident in the evidence store.

extensions.description: Organisation-specific fields. Validators ignore their content; keep evidence-bearing fields in the core record.
